subject: Checkout pause: availability audit and proposed compensatory calculation
messages:
From: Elena Torres <e.torres@fastcart.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 09:12:30 -0700
Subject: Checkout pause — urgent: we saw a 13m window of 503s during peak

Hi Soojin,

We saw a disruption this morning that impacted checkout on our US region: between roughly 08:58 and 09:11 PDT customers hit 503s and a number of carts were abandoned. Our telemetry shows a spike in failed API calls to your inference endpoint used in our fraud checkout step — that step is critical for completing payments.

Can you confirm whether Redwood experienced an availability gap in that window, and if eligible, what remedy/credit path looks like? We need a short timeline and any logs we can attach to our incident review and Finance.

Quick context: we process ~1.1M checkouts/day; in that 13-minute window we estimate ~0.6% of daily checkout volume failed. This is material for our revenue ops team.

Thanks — can you treat this as high priority?

Elena
Elena Torres

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 11:05:18 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout pause — urgent: we saw a 13m window of 503s during peak

Hi — I pulled the initial evidence for tenant fastcart-prod (endpoint /v1/infer/fraud-check). Summary below. Attaching a compact slice and traces.

Short verdict: there was a regional routing eviction affecting a subset of inference workers in us-west-2 that caused TTL refresh failures for the prefix cache; the runtime fell back to cold KV cache misses which caused elevated 5xx rates for about 12 minutes. We have captured trace-level spans and server logs.

Annotated timeline (UTC):
- 2028-07-24T15:58:12Z — First elevated 5xx detected on edge layer (p95 spike begins).
- 2028-07-24T15:59:03Z — Internal autoscaler triggered partial drain of two worker pools (eviction attempts).
- 2028-07-24T16:03:40Z — Fallback to cold-path increased CPU and queueing, p50->p95 widened significantly.
- 2028-07-24T16:10:24Z — Rolling recovery began as spare capacity came online and KV cache warmed.
- 2028-07-24T16:11:28Z — Observed 5xx rate returned to baseline.

This maps to FastCart local times: 08:58–09:11 PDT (approx). Root cause appears to be a concurrency between a localized host eviction event and a suboptimal autoscale policy for the worker pool serving that tenant pattern.

Attachments included (stubs):
- fastcart_log_slice_2028-07-24.tar.gz (logs + minimal trace snippets)
- p95_traces_2028-07-24.csv (span-level latencies)
- slo-window-annotated.png (timeline with annotated events)

Proposed next steps for eligibility and remedy:
1) We will produce a concise post-incident summary (RCAs) within 5 business days.
2) For initial compensatory math: based on our SLA (99.95% monthly availability), a 12-minute region-scoped unavailability in this tenant's production route would be eligible for prorated credit for the impacted window.
   - Example calculation: prorated credit = (downtime minutes / minutes in month) * monthly committed amount.
3) If FastCart would like an interim credit to help reconcile today's Finance review, we can offer a preliminary pro-rata credit estimate; final credit will be issued after the post-incident review confirms the impact window.

Please let me know if you want us to escalate this to a Severity 2 internal review immediately (we can pull additional raw KV cache dumps and kernel scheduling artifacts).

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Hi Elena —

Thank you for your patience. Ben confirmed an eviction-driven fallback that produced elevated 5xxs for approximately 12 minutes (we've attached the compact log slice and an annotated timeline). We take responsibility for the availability regression on our production route for the time window below.

Impacted window (Redwood's timeline): 2028-07-24T15:58:12Z -> 2028-07-24T16:10:24Z (≈12m).
Mapped to your local clock: ~08:58–09:11 PDT.

Preliminary compensatory proposal (interim):
- We will issue a provisional pro-rata credit equal to (12 minutes / 30 days) of the current monthly committed spend on your Dedicated plan (we calculated a preliminary estimate and can share exact numbers once you confirm the invoice id).
- This provisional credit will be reserved and finalized after our 5-business-day post-incident summary (RCA & mitigation plan). If the RCA changes the impact window materially, we'll adjust accordingly.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Final RCA and mitigation plan in 5 business days (target: 2028-07-31).
2) Ben's team will follow up with deeper artifacts if you request (KV cache dump and scheduler logs).
3) Laura will coordinate the credit issuance and timing with your billing contact — Laura, can you please reach out to ops@fastcart.com and let them know the provisional credit workflow and what you need to finalize the amount?

Elena, if you'd like a 20-minute sync this afternoon to review the evidence live I can jump on a call — otherwise we'll proceed by email and share the report by July 31.

Apologies again for the interruption. We'll also propose a short mitigation (autoscaler tuning + tenant-level warmup warmers) to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
